openings.claim: A thumb-actuated captive plunger might reseat the clip; guidance is predicted to align impulse with the clip axis and retain moving parts.
openings.discriminator: Adequate seating is predicted, with no performance ordering against the spring latch. Failure to seat, grip loss, or wiring contact defeats adequacy.
openings.probe: Proposed only: exercise orientations on a wiring surrogate; assess seating, retention, and grip.
openings.uncertainty: Captive-head concept is drawing-only; thumb force and guidance tolerance are unresolved.

openings.claim: A captive spring head with an elastomer latch may deliver repeatable taps; stored energy is predicted to reduce thumb-speed dependence.
openings.discriminator: Predicts less tap-to-tap variation than the plunger, without predicting higher seating success. Equivalent or greater variation defeats this comparison.
openings.probe: Proposed only: establish compatible latch-material availability, then compare repeated strokes on a surrogate.
openings.uncertainty: Indispensable compatible latch material availability and release stability are unknown; hard constraints still apply.

lineage.reason: Retains guided captive impulse, adequacy prediction, grip limits, and orientation probe.
Retains stored-energy mechanism, variation comparison, and indispensable material dependency.
Gravity-driven unattached weight can fall, violating retention even if seating succeeds. Energy sufficiency and wiring contact remain unresolved; no overhead trial proposed.

decision: Keep D1 and D2 as unconfirmed synthetic proposals; confirmation labels phase only. Clip geometry is hypothetical. Any candidate must reseat overhead while one hand operates and retains the device with a secure grip, no detached part may fall, and contact must avoid adjacent wiring. Establish D2 material feasibility before its comparative probe; no seating-success ranking is supported.
